blind_target.title: The beneficial and detrimental effects of major depression on intuitive decision-making.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The first hypothesis (H1) refers to the replicability of recently found intuition deficits in depression ( Remmers et al., 2015 ; Remmers et al., 2017 ).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Overall the current study did not replicate findings from previous research regarding intuitive semantic coherence detection deficits in depression.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The overall deficit replication verdict covers the two originals explicitly named for H1.

blind_target.title: The architecture of intuition: Fluency and affect determine intuitive judgments of semantic and visual coherence and judgments of grammaticality in artificial grammar learning.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Building up on basic research ( Topolinski & Strack, 2009a ; Experiment 8) showing that healthy subjects are more likely to judge triads to be coherent that consist of positive as compared to negative words, we expected that this effect would also emerge for depressed patients.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Results did not reveal any effect of our fluency manipulation, and thus our hypotheses regarding fluency (H2) were not supported. As such, the current study could not replicate previous results that bolstered the fluency model proposed by Topolinski and Strack (2009a , 2009b ).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Fluency comparison fails, while positive-valence comparison agrees. The fluency passage explicitly contrasts prior results. Additional agreement passage: The results further showed that positive (vs. negative) valence triggered coherence judgments (H3a) and that this effect was – in contrast to our hypothesis (H3b) – not moderated by depression.

shipped_originals.title_o: The Big Picture: Effects of Surround on Immersion and Size Perception

blind_target.evidence_quote: Moran et al. (2017, VSS) found that realistic miniature increased immersion relative to unrealistic miniatures, but memory was unaffected. However, the questions used to assess memory were very easy, raising the possibility of a ceiling effect. The current experiment was very similar to Moran et al. (2017).
blind_target.outcome_quote: However, immersion results failed to replicate: immersion scores did not significantly differ across the three conditions.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The title focuses on immersion and this effect explicitly failed. The prior memory null was also recovered; under the title-specific coding rule the central immersion finding is failed. The directly repeated study is Moran et al. (2017), not the earlier Baranowski and Hecht paper. No reference list is available to expand the citation.

shipped_originals.title_o: A LINGUISTIC STUDY OF CUES AND MISCUES IN READING.

blind_target.evidence_quote: The present study replicated the classic Goodman (1965) study, which found that children's reading accuracy improved 60%-80 % in context, in comparison with a list.
blind_target.outcome_quote: The results showed that the poor readers and the 6- and 7-year old average readers showed statistically reliable context gains in both experiments. However, the 6-year-old good readers and the 8-year-old average readers only gained reliably with context in the 2nd experiment. The 7-year-old good readers did not gain reliably with context in either experiment. The 8-year-old good readers made no reliable context gains in the 2nd experiment but gained reliably with the list in the 1st experiment.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly report context gains for poor and younger average readers, absent or reversed context gains for good readers and order-dependent gains for other groups. This qualifies the original result by subgroup; it is not merely a smaller effect.

shipped_originals.title_o: Culture's consequences: International differences in work-related values

blind_target.evidence_quote: This study replicates Hofstede’s study with data obtained from students studying for their master degrees in different universities in Jordan.
blind_target.outcome_quote: In conclusion we argue that Hofstede’s (1980, 1991, 2005) assumption that people who grow up in the same place will share similar views about life does not apply to his findings about Arab cultures and thus his generalization made to Jordanian culture is not validated.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The overall conclusion rejects the generalization to Jordan, which decides the verdict despite agreement on some dimensions.
